## Optimal Properties

Hicham TARIF Nadir MAAROUFI

March 2024

## Abstract

The main contribution of this paper is a constructive method for building separable multivariate vector-valued While separable wavelet bases in L? (Rd , R) are well-established and  widely applied, the explicit   construction of truly vector-valued   wavelet bases   remains even in the simplest In practice, the conventional approach applies standard separable wavelet bases of L? (R? , R) independently to each component of vector-valued signals in L? (R? , R2) . However; this approach fails to capture the intrinsic vectorial structure of the signals. To address this limitation, we propose a constructive approach within the vector-valued wavelet framework, providing systematic method for constructing such bases in the general case of L? (Rd , R") . By linking m-multiwavelets to vector-valued  wavelets; our approach not only enables the systematic construction of separable multivariate bases that satisfy the vector-valued multiresolution analysis but also ensures that these bases inherit structural properties; making them well-suited for practical applications. key

words Multivariate wavelet bases; Vector-valued wavelet bases; Vector-valued multiresolution decomposition; m-multiwavelets; Separable wavelets. Key

Yves Meyer's pioneering work on wavelets laid the foundation for Stéphane Mallat 's multiresolution analysis (MRA) in the scalar case\_ MRA provides a systematic and theoretical framework for constructing wavelet bases for spaces such as L2 (R) . A starting in MRA is to find scaling  function (father wavelet) that satisfies specific properties; from which the corresponding wavelet function (mother wavelet ) is derived [31]. This framework enables the decomposition of signals across multiple scales; facilitating analysis at various levels of resolution; and permitting the construction of a wavelet basis. MRA also provides a theoretical framework for constructing multivariate scalar wavelet bases in spaces such as L2 (Rd , R). However despite the general scheme of MRA, building such multivariate wavelet bases in practice remains challenging [27]- The primary difficulty lies in finding a suitable multivariate scaling point key

Significant advances in wavelet theory were achieved in the 1980s, notably by Yves Meyer [31] and Ingrid Daubechies [16]  Meyer's wavelets are constructed band-limited function; ensuring smoothness and regularity in the time domain.  Although they lack compact support; their smoothness and orthogonality make them suitable for applications requiring continuously differentiable wavelets\_ In contrast, Daubechies wavelets are constructed to possess compact support   and approximation of smooth functions. A advantage of Daubechies   wavelets is their ability to combine compact smooth function approximation; signal analysis; and image processing [16, 39, 38] The vanishing moments of the Daubechies wavelets play a crucial role in the multifractal formalism. More precisely; make the wavelets orthogonal to low-order polynomials, enabling the removal of such trends. Sequentially; wavelet transforms based on Daubechies wavelets characterize Hõlder spaces and pointwise regularity.
